reason: MANE and APPRIS agree on a 1,130-aa protein that adds 94 residues before the signal peptide of the 1,036-aa UniProt canonical. With the extension DeepTMHMM v1 no longer calls a signal peptide: it reads the signal peptide as a second TM helix and puts the N-terminus inside (2 TM, N-in; canonical: SP + 1 TM, N-out). The mouse and cyno models in L2 are also 1,130 aa, so the extension may be translated, but nothing in this audit shows the extended protein reaching the surface. The 1,036-aa reviewed UniProt form has a clean, cleavable signal peptide at residue 1 and the canonical type I topology, which is the form a surface-display library needs. Met95 is a native ATG, so the repair is a 5' trim with no codon edit.
alternative_rejected: keep the 1,130-aa MANE / APPRIS form with its 94-residue extension

decided_by: l1-proteoform-audit (delegated by Becca 2026-11-12, "use your best judgment")
implemented_by: Claude Code session l1-proteoform-audit, PR #300 (branch claude/l1-proteoform-audit-c4b011)
reason: The cyno Ensembl 116 model starts 31 residues upstream of the residue aligned to human Met1, which is an in-frame, native ATG (ortholog Met32). The extension is not in the human protein, carries no signal peptide (DeepTMHMM v1) and would sit on the extracellular N-terminus, where the tag goes. Ensembl 116 has no other model for this cyno gene. Starting at Met32 makes the protein exactly as long as the human reference, which marks the extension as a gene-model error. The repair is a 5' trim to a native codon; no codon is edited. It is an explicit, recorded exception to the ortholog CDS policy's ban on implicit start repairs.
alternative_rejected: redraw from the Compara 116 pool (loses the cyno CHRM3 arm)
